subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should OpenClaw support recurring isolated cron jobs that clean up their run sessions by default, or should `deleteAfterRun` remain a one-shot-only lifecycle contract?
rationale: This PR and the open strict-validation PR encode opposite cron lifecycle semantics, and the correct upgrade behavior for existing persisted omitted jobs depends on that product contract.

options.title: Support recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require persisted-row/load or doctor coverage so existing omitted recurring isolated jobs also clean up after upgrade.

options.title: Make deleteAfterRun one-shot-only
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue through the strict-validation path after Gateway/UI caller and recovery gaps are fixed.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only behavior
options.body: Land only the new-create default and explicitly document that existing omitted jobs need operator action or a separate migration.

recommendation.title: Support recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require persisted-row/load or doctor coverage so existing omitted recurring isolated jobs also clean up after upgrade.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main cron normalization/store history points there, and this is a core compatibility/product contract choice rather than a narrow cleanup-helper decision.
